_about: Hand-labelled ground truth for golang-jwt/jwt (Go), auth0/java-jwt (Java),
OpenSSL (C) and rustls (Rust) - four further real-world corpora this project did not author.
Produced by reading each library's shipped (non-test) source, NOT from ECDAT output.
These exist so the multi-language claim is measured rather than asserted.
method: Each labelled file is read by a human reviewer and the expected set of algorithms is written down from the source, before any detector runs. A label states what the FILE uses, at the granularity the source actually states: where a construction is generic over its digest (an HMAC over a caller-chosen hash, an HKDF over a generic MAC) the label names the construction WITHOUT a digest, because naming one would be a claim the file does not make. Where a source states a key size the size is part of the label. Labels are never edited to match detector output; a disagreement is recorded as a disagreement.

labelled_files.reviewer_notes: Registers SigningMethodHS256/384/512 as &SigningMethodHMAC{...crypto.SHA256}. The family is chosen by a struct literal naming a crypto.Hash constant, so the JOSE name and the digest are both declaration-level.
SigningMethodRS256/384/512 over crypto.SHA256/384/512. Key size is the caller's, so the family is RSA without a fixed modulus.
PS256/384/512 - RSASSA-PSS, a distinct scheme from PKCS#1 v1.5. Must not be merged into the RSA-2048 surface.
ES256/384/512 with curve byte sizes 32/48/66.
SigningMethodEdDSA over ed25519. Post-quantum secure - the only PQ-safe scheme in the library.

SigningMethodNone, the unsecured JWT algorithm. Deliberately shipped behind SigningMethodNone.RequireExplicitAllowance() in v5. Its presence in the inventory is the point: an auditor must be able to see it exists and see the guard.

labelled_files.negative_reason: Token parsing and claim extraction. Selects a signing method through the registry but names no primitive.
Claim validation (expiry, not-before, issuer, audience). No cryptography.
Struct and interface declarations for tokens and claims.
Registry plumbing: RegisterSigningMethod / GetSigningMethod. Names no algorithm.

labelled_files.reviewer_notes: The factory class. Every JOSE name is bound to a JCA provider name as a string literal: new RSAAlgorithm("RS256", "SHA256withRSA", ...), new RSAAlgorithm("PS256", "RSASSA-PSS", pssParams("SHA-256",...), ...), new HMACAlgorithm("HS256", "HmacSHA256", ...), ECAlgorithm("ES256", "SHA256withECDSA", SECP256R1), and new NoneAlgorithm() at :441. RSA-PSS is a distinct scheme from PKCS#1 v1.5 and is inventoried separately. The primitive is chosen by the JCA provider at runtime, so the literal is the only declaration.

The JCA boundary. Signature.getInstance(algorithm) and Mac.getInstance(algorithm) at :157,:209,:235,:255,:302. The name arrives as a parameter, so no specific algorithm can be named here - the class is a cryptographic primitive boundary, and that is what the label records.

labelled_files.negative_reason: Sign/verify driver. Delegates to CryptoHelper with a name held in a field. No primitive named in this file.
As HMACAlgorithm - the JCA name was already declared in Algorithm.java where the object is constructed.
As HMACAlgorithm. Also carries a JWSSignatureFormat dependency for DER<->concat conversion, which is encoding rather than cryptography.

labelled_files.reviewer_notes: The unsecured algorithm, shipped as Algorithm.none(). Signature verification is a no-op by construction. Correctly critical.

labelled_files.negative_reason: Token assembly. Calls Algorithm.sign(), which is polymorphic across the families already inventoried in Algorithm.java.

labelled_files.reviewer_notes: The MD5 compression function itself. MD5_Init and md5_block_data_order; the RFC1321 constants are the IV, not a key.
SHA256_Init/Update/Transform/Final plus SHA224_Init, which truncates the same core. A 192-bit truncation is also compiled.
SHA1_Init/Update/Final and ossl_sha1_ctrl. The ctrl path composes a SHA-1 with an inner and outer hash.

The HMAC construction itself, generic over the digest: HMAC_Init_ex takes an EVP_MD *md parameter. The digest is a caller's choice, so the MAC is reported WITHOUT a digest - naming one would be a claim the file does not make.
DES_encrypt1/2 operate on one key schedule (single DES). DES_encrypt3 takes three schedules, which is Triple-DES EDE - a different and separately deprecated algorithm.
BF_encrypt, the 16/20-round Blowfish core. BF_ROUNDS selects 16 or 20.

The EVP AES table. Key size and mode are macro arguments (BLOCK_CIPHER_generic_pack(NID_aes, 128, 0)), not identifiers, so a detector must read the argument rather than the NID. GCM, XTS, CCM and wrap variants are also declared.

The digest-to-HMAC pairing table: NID_sha1->NID_hmacWithSHA1 and so on, including the truncated SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 variants and the four SHA-3 sizes. Every name here is a registry identifier; no primitive is invoked.

corpora.name: rustls 0.24.0-dev (Rust)
corpora.corpus_note: Eight shipped files from the rustls workspace: three from the provider-agnostic main crate (rustls/src/crypto/{hash,hmac,tls13}.rs) and five from the ring provider (rustls-ring/src/{hash,hmac,sign,tls12,tls13}.rs). These files are byte-identical to upstream except that `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks were removed, matching the non-test convention used for every other corpus here. The sha256 of every ORIGINAL upstream file is recorded in fixtures/rustls_repo/.upstream_hashes.json so the derivation is checkable. Stripping the test modules removed exactly one algorithm from the corpus: HMAC-SHA512 in rustls-ring/src/tls12.rs, which is referenced only from a RFC 7627 test vector. That is why tls12.rs below does not expect it.

labelled_files.negative_reason: Interface only. The file declares `pub trait Hash` and the `Output`/`Context` value types. It never binds a digest - the algorithm arrives as a return value of `Hash::algorithm()`. A trait declaration that names no algorithm is not a selection of one, so a detector that reported a digest here would be inventing it.
labelled_files.reviewer_notes: SHA256 appears only inside a doc comment, which is not code.

labelled_files.negative_reason: Interface only. The file declares `pub trait Hmac`, `Key`, and the `Tag` value types. No HMAC is constructed here and no digest is bound: `Key::sign_concat` is a method the provider must implement. The doc comment naming HMAC-SHA256/SHA384 is prose, not a binding.
labelled_files.reviewer_notes: Contrast with the ring provider's hmac.rs, which does bind digests.

Implements the HKDF construction: `HkdfUsingHmac` and `HkdfExpanderUsingHmac` implement Hkdf/HkdfExpander/HkdfPrkExtract per RFC 5869, looping `sign_concat` to produce T(i) = HMAC(PRK, T(i-1) | info | i). The MAC is a `dyn hmac::Hmac` chosen by the caller, so HKDF is labelled WITHOUT a digest. HMAC itself is not labelled here: this file delegates to the HMAC abstraction rather than implementing it.

`pub(crate) static SHA256: Hash = Hash(&digest::SHA256, HashAlgorithm::SHA256)` and the same for SHA384. The `struct Hash` wrapper is the concrete implementation of rustls::crypto::hash::Hash over ring's digest context.

Three statics binding ring's algorithms: `Hmac(&hmac::HMAC_SHA256)`, `HMAC_SHA384`, `HMAC_SHA512`. SHA512 carries an `#[allow(dead_code)]` comment saying it is used by a TLS 1.2 PRF test and the aws-lc-rs HPKE suites - it is still non-test code in this file, so it is labelled.

The signing-key provider. RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256/384/512 and RSA-PSS with SHA-256/384/512 are bound as `signature::RSA_PKCS1_SHA*` / `signature::RSA_PSS_SHA*`; ECDSA is bound per curve via `SignatureScheme::ECDSA_NISTP{256,384}_SHA*` and `alg_id::ECDSA_P{256,384}` plus the `ECDSA_P*_ASN1_SIGNING` encoding algorithms; Ed25519 via `alg_id::ED25519`. RSA is labelled WITHOUT a key size because the file states none - `alg_id::RSA_ENCRYPTION` is a PKCS#1 algorithm identifier and the key length is the caller's choice.

The six TLS 1.2 cipher suites. Record protection is `aead::AES_128_GCM`, `aead::AES_256_GCM` and `aead::CHACHA20_POLY1305`; the PRF is `PrfUsingHmac(&super::hmac::HMAC_SHA{256,384})`; the transcript hash is `super::hash::SHA{256,384}`. TLS12_ECDSA_SCHEMES lists ED25519 and the NIST P-256/384/521 signature schemes; TLS12_RSA_SCHEMES lists the PSS and PKCS#1 schemes. HMAC-SHA512 is NOT expected: in this file it appears only inside the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block, exercising an RFC 7627 vector, and the non-test corpus convention removes it.

The three TLS 1.3 cipher suites. `RingHkdf(hkdf::HKDF_SHA256, hmac::HMAC_SHA256)` and the SHA384 pair, so HKDF is bound to a digest here and both the KDF and the MAC are labelled. The record AEADs are `aead::AES_128_GCM`, `aead::AES_256_GCM` and `aead::CHACHA20_POLY1305`, with the QUIC header-protection algorithms (`aead::quic::AES_128`, `AES_256`, `CHACHA20`) being the same primitives under a different construction, not additional algorithms.
